editorial_thesis: The useful frontier is the control plane: task-scoped authority, layered execution boundaries, and accepted-artifact measurement are what make more capable agents deployable.

topic_groups.title: Governed Agent Operations
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Fresh September 9 implementation signal: enterprise controls now govern agent operations at the shell, file, network, and code-quality layers rather than only approving the overall tool.

sources.title: Enterprise managed permissions for Copilot agent operations
sources.why_selected: It turns agent authority into a typed policy surface that users cannot weaken with local auto-approval or saved approvals.
sources.usefulness: Model Buildn tool permissions as deny / ask / allow by operation, target, and workspace rather than one global “trusted agent” switch.

sources.title: Agentic autofix for code-quality findings
sources.why_selected: Batching turns security debt into a queue while preserving a branch and human merge decision.
sources.usefulness: Offer a client “safe backlog burn-down” pilot: only standard findings, one PR batch, explicit validation, and measured reviewer time.

sources.title: CodeQL 2.27.0 adds Linux ARM64 support
sources.why_selected: Security scanning can follow lower-cost or edge-oriented build infrastructure instead of forcing every repository onto x86 runners.
sources.usefulness: Add architecture to the security-matrix inventory for self-hosted runners and client CI migrations.

sources.title: Block pull requests with exposed secrets from merging
sources.why_selected: It moves secret detection from notification to a delivery gate, where an agent’s generated patch must satisfy the same safety rule as human code.
sources.usefulness: Make “no exposed secret” a hard acceptance check for generated artifacts and integration changes.

sources.title: GitHub Advanced Security expands trial availability
sources.why_selected: A short trial can produce evidence about finding volume, remediation throughput, and review load before a broader commitment.
sources.usefulness: Package a one-week “agent + security” assessment for a client with baseline and post-pilot metrics.

topic_groups.title: Safe Agent Code Execution
topic_groups.selection_rationale: A fresh infrastructure essay plus new sandbox placement options sharpen a neglected gap: safe execution is a control-plane problem, not a container checkbox.

sources.title: What infrastructure do AI agents need to run code safely?
sources.why_selected: It makes the hidden operational dependencies visible: a container does not decide credentials, network reach, expiry, cleanup, or promotion.
sources.usefulness: Use the eight layers as a Buildn/client architecture-review checklist for any agent that executes code or touches private data.

sources.title: Cursor Cloud Agents can run in Vercel Sandbox
sources.why_selected: Execution location becomes a deployment choice: teams can align sandbox region, account boundary, observability, and cost with the rest of the application.
sources.usefulness: Test a client prototype where the agent runs in the same governed environment as preview artifacts, but cannot promote directly.

sources.title: Vercel Sandbox routing is 18× faster globally
sources.why_selected: Lower routing latency matters for interactive agent loops and short-lived preview environments, especially when the work is distributed geographically.
sources.usefulness: Measure whether faster sandbox readiness changes perceived quality for browser QA or preview-driven client work.

sources.title: Persistent memory for eve agents
sources.why_selected: Memory becomes a declared storage component with an ownership boundary instead of an invisible prompt trick.
sources.usefulness: Borrow the provider/scope split for Buildn: workspace memory, user memory, and task memory should have distinct retention and deletion rules.

sources.title: Sandbox architecture: promote artifacts, not mutable runtimes
sources.why_selected: This separates experimentation from deployment and prevents a compromised or drifted runtime from becoming the release authority.
sources.usefulness: Make every Buildn agent return a patch, report, or bundle with provenance; a human or separate pipeline owns promotion.

topic_groups.title: Frontier Work Surfaces
topic_groups.selection_rationale: A current model launch and workspace-agent product surface make this a material update to recent model-portfolio coverage: the differentiator is using existing tools and accepting measurable work, not just selecting a larger model.

sources.title: GPT-6 Astra: the next generation in intelligence for work
sources.why_selected: The practical claim is reduced integration work: the model can operate through existing applications even when no API exists.
sources.usefulness: Run one bounded client workflow where the output is a reviewed deck, spreadsheet, or code change—not an untracked action sequence.

sources.title: Introducing Workspace Agents in ChatGPT
sources.why_selected: The unit of adoption shifts from an individual prompt to a reusable team process with permissions, memory, and continuous correction.
sources.usefulness: Model a Buildn dossier agent as a shared workflow: sources in, cited draft out, explicit publication approval.

sources.title: GPT-6 Astra now available on Vercel AI Gateway
sources.why_selected: A common gateway reduces the cost of a controlled trial and makes model selection a routing configuration rather than a rewrite.
sources.usefulness: Run the same acceptance suite through the existing gateway, keeping prompts, tools, and artifact checks constant.

sources.title: Research acceleration: accepted work over token volume
sources.why_selected: It gives a better ROI unit for agents: accepted artifacts and reviewer time, not raw calls, tokens, or generated text.
sources.usefulness: Use accepted report sections, merged patches, and resolved issues as Buildn delivery metrics.

sources.title: Workspace agents as durable process, not chat history
sources.why_selected: The durable asset is the tested process and its guardrails; the chat transcript is only one invocation.
sources.usefulness: Create versioned agent briefs with owner, data scope, approval points, and rollback instructions.
